criteria.criterion: A peer reconverge does not return or emit an `fsck-recover` warning solely because a lock-owning push recovery merge has created `MERGE_HEAD`.
After the push recovery merge releases the lock, both operations exit successfully, `MERGE_HEAD` is absent, the lock is clear, local and remote tips match, and all seeded events remain reachable.
A stranded merge marker found after lock acquisition still blocks reset or merge mutation and directs the operator to `rebar fsck-recover`.
Fetch remains outside the store write lock, and existing fetch coordination and best-effort lock timeout behavior remain unchanged.
The regression test uses synchronization barriers instead of a wall-clock race.
Focused tests, lint, type checking, and the full suite pass.
Bug 'sync.reconverge misclassifies a lock-owned push recovery merge as abandoned' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.

findings.criterion: Focused tests, lint, type checking, and the full suite pass.
findings.detail: This criterion requires running the test suite, linter, and type checker — operational evidence that cannot be verified from the repository alone. The tests themselves exist in the codebase (test_reconverge_waits_for_a_lock_owned_push_recovery_merge and test_reconverge_refuses_a_stranded_merge_marker_after_lock_acquisition are both present and well-formed), but no concrete attestation with a CI run ID, log URL, or observed outcome is visible in the ticket snapshot I read.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment naming the specific CI run URL/ID, the observed outcome (all tests green, lint clean, type check clean), and the date/time of the run.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
